Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 4 -

5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through - 5 - the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not fulfilled properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victim of violence is a Woman who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victim of violence is a Child who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or - 27 -
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
5. The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 43

1. Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. Victims;
b. Family;
c. Community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle victims of violence against Women and Children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regional Regulation.

Paragraph 6

Social

Article 51

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is aimed at returning Women and Child victims of violence to their area of origin.
2. Repatriation of victims of violence of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Child victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

29 -

Article 49

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions of law enforcement officials provided to Women and Child victims of violence and/or witnesses.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

28 -

Article 24

Children in formal and non-formal educational institution environments must be protected from acts of violence.

Article 19

1. Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.

Article 20

1. Female workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and  b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace.
4. Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

1. The Regency Government is obligated to provide care for neglected Children.

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or - 27 -
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
5. The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regional Regulation.

1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 4 -

5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through - 5 - the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not fulfilled properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victim of violence is a Woman who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victim of violence is a Child who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
(2) Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or - 27 -
d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
5. The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regional Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency. 4 -

5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through - 5 - the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not fulfilled properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victim of violence is a Woman who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victim of violence is a Child who experiences actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Article 36

1. The Regency Government is obligated to provide care for neglected Children.
2. Care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social field.
3. In the event that a Child is neglected due to a reason that the parents neglect their obligations, then the Family or Regency Government or Community Organization as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
4. The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) simultaneously determines the place of shelter and care for the neglected Child concerned.

CHAPTER VIII

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 55

1. Every Child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.

30 - (2) Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted through Child Forums starting from the village level, sub-district within the regency.

3. Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent Children, both geographic domicile representation, socio-cultural groups and Children's educational backgrounds.
4. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) is facilitated by the Regency Government.
(5) The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (4) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.
